findings.title: connectedCalendars handler bypasses the feature-flag/mock and queries calendarCache unconditionally
findings.body: The handler instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly and calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` on every `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query. Everywhere else in the codebase the repository is obtained via `CalendarCache.init(null)`, which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the calendar-cache feature flag is disabled. By constructing the repository directly, this handler (a) runs an extra `groupBy` query against the `CalendarCache` table on every calendar-settings page load even for instances/teams where the feature is off, and (b) makes the newly added `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` implementation on the mock dead code — the mock will never be consulted here. Use the same init/feature-flag path as the rest of the calendar-cache code so the query is skipped when the feature is disabled.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars type widened to require updatedAt/googleChannelId that nothing in this module consumes
findings.body: `UserWithCalendars` now requires `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on both `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars`, but neither field is read anywhere in `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` or its helpers in this file (the only consumer of the new `updatedAt` write is the frontend reading `CalendarCache.updatedAt` instead, per the PR's own notes). Only `findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated to select the new fields; any other caller of this widely-used function (it is re-exported as `getConnectedDestinationCalendars` for `@calcom/platform-libraries`, plus tests/fixtures constructing this type) that builds the user object without these fields will now fail type-checking. Either consume the fields or revert the type widening to avoid a needless contract break.

findings.title: deleteCache handler throws a generic Error instead of a TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential is not found or doesn't belong to the user, the handler does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC converts a generic `Error` into an `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (HTTP 500), so clients see a server error for what is actually a not-found/forbidden condition, and it may get reported as an unexpected server fault. Throw a `TRPCError` with code `NOT_FOUND` (or `FORBIDDEN`) to match the convention used elsewhere in the codebase.

findings.title: Unconditional empty updateMany write to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt whose value is never read
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now ends with `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, an `updateMany` with empty data whose only effect is to touch `updatedAt` on every SelectedCalendar row for the credential. This runs on the webhook/cache-refresh hot path, yet the PR description itself notes that `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not displayed or read anywhere (the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt` via `cacheUpdatedAt`). This is a dead write on a hot path; either remove it or wire it to an actual consumer before merging. Additionally, the method's parameter is typed `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` while `updateMany` expects `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput` — it only compiles because `{}` is passed; any real payload with relation fields would be a type error.

findings.title: Dev script uses macOS-only `sed -i ''` and a cwd-relative .env path
findings.body: Two portability/correctness issues in the new helper script: (1) `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax — on GNU/Linux `sed -i ''` treats the empty string as a filename and the script fails with "can't read : No such file or directory", so the script silently breaks for Linux developers. (2) `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the caller's current working directory, not the script's location; running it from anywhere other than the `scripts/` directory will create or modify a `.env` in an unintended parent directory. Resolve the env file relative to the script's own path (e.g. via `$(dirname "$0")`).

findings.title: Cache 'last updated' timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale
findings.body: The cache status line formats the timestamp with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, ignoring the user's configured locale even though `useLocale()` is already available in the component. Non-US users will see US date/time formatting in a user-facing settings page, inconsistent with the rest of the app. Pass the user's locale (e.g. `i18n.language` from `useLocale`) or use the app's existing date-formatting helpers.
